paper_title: Thinking Slow, Fast Scaling Inference Compute with Distilled Reasoners
caption_used: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the coverage achieved as a function of the number of completions (k). The x-axis is logarithmic, ranging from 2^0 to 2^8, with tick labels spaced by powers of 2. The y-axis represents coverage, with values ranging from approximately 0.22 to 0.92. A solid blue line represents the Llama-3B model, beginning at approximately 0.42 coverage when k=20 and increasing to approximately 0.92 coverage at k=256. A dashed green line displays the Llama-3B + FT model, which starts at approximately 0.22 coverage when k=20 and reaches approximately 0.72 coverage at k=128. A light blue line represents the Llama-1B model, starting at approximately 0.22 coverage when k=20 and reaching approximately 0.72 coverage at k=128. A dotted light green line displays the Llama-1B + FT model, which also begins at approximately 0.22 coverage when k=20 and plateaus at approximately 0.68 coverage at k=128.
